sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface staining confirmed extracellular display of the Myc tag on full-length membrane-anchored PCDHGA1; no quantitative functional assay (e.g., homophilic binding, synapse formation) reported specifically for the tagged construct in L5.
sites.rationale: L5 (PMC12337331) and L6 (PMC12157453) both report a Myc tag placed in the extracellular stalk between EC6 and the TM helix of full-length cPCDH constructs including PCDHGA1, confirmed by surface staining; neither paper names a specific residue number, so the site is region-level. The stalk spans roughly residues 650–690 (all extracellular, ≥3 residues from TM start at 693), making it sterically accessible for a short epitope tag. L5 is used as the primary clip; L6 independently corroborates the same region and approach. Full-length PCDHGA1 (and other cPCDH isoforms) expressed in mammalian cells with a Myc tag placed in the extracellular stalk between EC6 and the TM helix; surface staining of the intact membrane-anchored protein was performed to confirm extracellular display.

sources.claim: For derived constructs including the Myc tag, the tag was positioned in the stalk region between EC6 and the transmembrane helix ( SI Appendix , Fig.

literature_notes: L1–L4 all describe C-terminal mCherry fusions (pCMV-mCherry-N1 vector = tag at the protein C-terminus, residue 931), which is deep within the intracellular domain (IC: 714–931). These are intracellular tags and do not qualify as extracellular surface sites; they are recorded in other_positions. L5 and L6 describe the same stalk-region Myc insertion in identical language and do not pin separate junctions, so they constitute one site. No specific residue number is given in either L5 or L6, so insert_after_residue is null and the site is classified as region-level with position_evidence='inferred'.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal mCherry fusion (pCMV-mCherry-N1) places the tag after residue 931, which is within the intracellular domain (IC: 714–931); confirmed functional in neurons but not an extracellular surface tag.
